q-72754.problem_mask:
![](images/38/38e096b8d57404135b7fe3244e50989e66021f94bb2275c56956d8663575b4f8.png)

Rounded to the nearest integer, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
q-72754.solution_mask:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

First we find the area for $△ABD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {{a}}\cdot {{b}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}{{{theta}}}^{∘} \\  & ={{h1}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}{{{theta}}}^{∘} \\  & \approx {{v1}},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot {{c}}\cdot {{d}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}{{{phi}}}^{∘} \\  & ={{h2}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}{{{phi}}}^{∘} \\  & \approx {{v2}},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & ={{v1}}+{{v2}} \\  & ={{total}}\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest integer, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is ${{answer}}.$

Rounded to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram $ABCD$ is{{field-1}}.
q-279762.solution_mask:
The diagonal $\overset{―}{AC}$ divides the parallelogram into two congruent triangles. Therefore, the area of the parallelogram is twice the area of $△ACB$ (see the illustration below).

![](images/b1/b1d0cf7c5a7c6ad7f0f52c8686239920fabcb05be57372ae0c7c9c9491838a52.png)

 Computing the area of $△ACB,$ we find
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ACB} & =\frac{1}{2}({{a}})({{b}})\operatorname{sin}⁡{{{theta}}}^{∘} \\  & ={{h1}}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{{{theta}}}^{∘} \\  & ≈{{v1}},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places. Consequently,

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & =2{A}_{ACB} \\  & =2\cdot {{v1}} \\  & ={{total}}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, to the **nearest integer**, the area of the parallelogram is ${{answer}}.$
